chapter: Corrections and views on early Black music
title: Dr. Locke's book and the record of early Black bands
summary: White says Locke should retract his statements and that his own travels give him knowledge of the bands.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Critics, polls and the jazz press

blocks.x: Oh, yes. Different. But I'll say this much for them, they were great fellows. Now, all those men that were down there that established historical things in music. Somebody up here at Howard University or a Ninnicka poop around New York or a denounce it. No, no. I don't like that at all. Dr. Locke should retract every statement he uttered in his book, because none of it is true. I've told you about the band in Savannah. I've told you about the musicians down in Florida. I've told you about them in Pensacola, North of Virginia, St. Louis, all around. Well, Jenkins' band had gone and heard these musicians, so we know. We were better to give you the historical data of it than somebody like him. His foot's behind a desk in Howard University. There is where it should stay. He's delving into the face of something he doesn't know anything about. That's not the law. By the way, I think he's dead.
I'm quite sure he died a couple years or more. Anyhow, he put out a little book. Yes.
I'm pretty sure he's dead now.
Well, anyway, I read that book years ago.
